chunks: And by this chain, from Yunus, from Sabbah al-Muzani, from Abu Hamzah, from one of the two عليهمَا السَّلَامُ, regarding the saying of Allah, Majestic and Mighty,
“Yes! Whoever earns an evil deed and his sin encompasses him.”
He said: “When he denies the Imamate of Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام,”
“then those are the companions of the Fire; they shall abide therein forever.”

key_terms.أَصْحَابُ النَّارِ: the inhabitants or companions of the Fire
key_terms.أَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: title of Imam Ali عليه السلام
key_terms.إِمَامَةَ: the divinely appointed leadership and authority
key_terms.خَطِيئَتُهُ: his sin that surrounds and overtakes him
key_terms.سَيِّئَةً: an evil deed or grave sin

ai.seo_question: How is Qur'an 2:81 interpreted in Shia hadith regarding the Imamate of Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith presents an interpretation of the verse by linking the encompassing sin to denial of the Imamate of Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام. It frames the verse as a warning about a grave theological rejection whose consequence is abiding in the Fire.
